objectives.statement: Relate eyelid protection, tear spreading and medial drainage to the arrangement of the ocular adnexa.
Identify the palpebral aperture, canthi, sulcus, caruncle, plica and puncta in clinical orientation.
Explain how lashes and lid-margin sensory input support the blink reflex.
Relate the orbital, palpebral and lacrimal portions of orbicularis oculi to closure and the tear pump.
Predict upper-lid findings after levator palpebrae superioris or oculomotor dysfunction.
Relate sympathetic supply of the superior tarsal muscle to mild ptosis in Horner syndrome.
Trace the principal anterior-to-posterior tissue layers of the upper eyelid.
Explain how the tarsal plate and canthal attachments stabilize the eyelids.
Relate meibomian secretion to tear-film lipid and evaporative stability.
Distinguish palpebral, forniceal and bulbar conjunctiva and the contribution of goblet cells.
Differentiate the glands of Zeiss, Moll, Krause and Wolfring by location and secretion.
Compare lower-lid support and mobility with the upper lid and relate laxity to tear drainage.
Trace the principal arterial arcades and venous drainage of the eyelids and conjunctiva.
Describe the superolateral location, orbital and palpebral parts, acini and excretory ducts of the lacrimal gland.
Relate lacrimal arterial and venous supply to orbital anatomy.
Trace parasympathetic secretomotor and sympathetic vasomotor pathways to the lacrimal gland.
Relate tear-film components to stability and interpret Schirmer and tear-break-up testing.
Trace tears from the ocular surface through the lacrimal passages to the inferior nasal meatus.

questions.author: OpenAI Codex (draft author)
questions.sampleAnswer: Meibomian dysfunction increases evaporation, incomplete blinking worsens distribution and pump action, and punctal malposition reduces drainage. The combination can cause unstable vision, irritation and paradoxical overflow.
rubric: Links meibomian lipid loss to evaporation.
Links blinking to tear distribution and lacrimal pumping.

questions.stem: Create a concise anatomical explanation for a patient whose lacrimal secretion falls after a lesion of the greater petrosal nerve but remains less affected after selective sympathetic loss.
questions.explanation: The corrected physiology distinguishes dominant parasympathetic secretion from chiefly vasomotor sympathetic influence.

Anatomy, Head and Neck: Eye Tear Film

questions.author: OpenAI Codex (draft author)
questions.sampleAnswer: The greater petrosal nerve carries preganglionic parasympathetic secretomotor fibres to the pterygopalatine ganglion. These fibres provide dominant secretomotor drive. Sympathetic fibres arrive through the deep petrosal nerve and are mainly vasomotor or modulatory, so their loss has a smaller secretory effect.
rubric: Traces the greater petrosal parasympathetic route.
